name: Tomato soup
summary: Smooth tomato soup with soft onion, carrot and celery, finished with basil.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and gently cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, stock and sugar, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the basil and blend until smooth. Season with black pepper and stir in the single cream if using.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Freeze before adding the cream. Ready-made stock is salted, so taste before adding any salt. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Vegetable soup
summary: Chunky soup of root vegetables, leek and peas in a light vegetable stock.
method: Dice the onion, leek, carrots, celery, potatoes and swede into roughly 1 cm pieces and crush the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion, leek, carrots and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until starting to soften. Add the garlic, dried thyme and bay leaves for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, swede and stock, bring to the boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 to 25 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Add the frozen peas for the last 3 minutes. Remove the bay leaves, season with black pepper and stir in the parsley.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Weigh the potatoes and swede after peeling. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Chicken vegetable soup
summary: Chunky root vegetable and leek soup with chicken thighs simmered in chicken stock and shredded.
method: Dice the onion, leek, carrots, celery, potatoes and swede into roughly 1 cm pieces and crush the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion, leek, carrots and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until starting to soften. Add the garlic, dried thyme and bay leaves for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, swede, whole chicken thighs and chicken stock, bring to the boil and simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables tender.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pan with the frozen peas for 3 minutes. Remove the bay leaves, season with black pepper and stir in the parsley.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: The vegetable soup with chicken thighs and chicken stock. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Minestrone
summary: Italian-style vegetable soup with tomato, cannellini beans and small pasta.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and gently cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the diced courgette, the green beans cut into short lengths, the chopped tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cannellini beans and the dry small pasta and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes more until the pasta is tender, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Season with black pepper, stir in the torn basil and top with the Parmesan if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Any small pasta shape works; macaroni is used for the nutrition. To freeze, freeze it before adding the pasta. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Chicken noodle soup
summary: Classic chicken soup with carrots, celery and egg noodles in a thyme-scented broth.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the chopped onion, sliced carrots and celery for 8 minutes until softening. Add the garlic, dried thyme and bay leaves for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken stock, add the whole chicken breasts and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through. Lift them out and shred with two forks.
Break the dry egg noodles into the soup and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until tender. Return the chicken, remove the bay leaves and add the parsley, black pepper and the lemon juice if using.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: The noodles keep softening as the soup stands; if making ahead, cook them separately. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Pumpkin soup
summary: Velvety blended pumpkin soup with onion, garlic and a hint of nutmeg.
method: Peel and deseed the pumpkin and cut it into chunks; weigh it after preparing.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the pumpkin, stock and nutmeg.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the pumpkin is very soft, then blend until smooth and season with black pepper.
Swirl in the single cream and scatter with toasted pumpkin seeds if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Freeze before adding the cream. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Carrot and coriander soup
summary: Smooth carrot soup with ground and fresh coriander.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ground coriander and stir for 1 minute.
Add the sliced carrots, the peeled and diced potato and the stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Add most of the fresh coriander and blend until smooth. Season with black pepper and scatter over the rest of the coriander.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Leek and potato soup
summary: Smooth soup of slowly softened leeks and potatoes, finished with milk.
method: Slice the leeks, wash well and drain. Chop the onion and peel and dice the potatoes.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan, add the leeks and onion, cover and sweat on a low heat for 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are falling apart.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk, warm through and season with black pepper. Top with snipped chives if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Mushroom soup
summary: Creamy blended soup of browned chestnut mushrooms with thyme.
method: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic, sliced mushrooms and dried thyme and cook over a medium-high heat for 10 minutes until the mushrooms have released their liquid and browned.
Stir in the plain flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock, stirring. Bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth, or leave some texture, then stir in the single cream and parsley, warm through and season with black pepper.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Broccoli soup
summary: Bright green blended broccoli and potato soup, with cheddar stirred through if you like.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 6 to 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the peeled and diced potato and the stock and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the broccoli, cut into small florets with the stalk sliced, and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes more until just tender.
Blend until smooth and season with black pepper. Stir the grated cheddar through until melted if using.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Lentil and tomato soup
summary: Smooth, tomato-rich red lentil soup with softened red pepper, a little chilli and basil.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the chopped onion, carrot and red pepper for 10 to 12 minutes until soft and starting to colour at the edges. Add the garlic, chilli flakes and tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed dry red lentils, the chopped tomatoes, stock and sugar. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have broken down completely.
Add the basil and blend until completely smooth, loosening with a little water if needed. Season with black pepper.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: A smooth, tomato-led soup, unlike the chunky brown lentil soup in the vegetarian family. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: White bean and rosemary soup
summary: Rustic cannellini bean soup with rosemary and kale, half blended for body.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and gently cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes. Add the sliced garlic and finely chopped rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the cannellini beans and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend about half the soup and stir it back in to thicken. Add the shredded kale and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Stir in the lemon juice, season with black pepper and top with the Parmesan if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Two 400 g tins of cannellini beans, drained. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Pea and mint soup
summary: Bright green blended soup of frozen peas and fresh mint.
method: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the peeled and diced potato and the stock and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the frozen peas, bring back to the boil and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the mint and blend until smooth. Season with black pepper.
Top each bowl with a spoonful of crème fraîche if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Freeze before adding the crème fraîche. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Fish soup
summary: Tomato and fennel broth with potatoes, chunks of cod and prawns.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and gently cook the chopped onion and fennel for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, bay leaves and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine if using and let it bubble for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes, fish stock and peeled, diced potatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the cod, cut into large chunks, and the peeled prawns, and simmer very gently for 4 to 5 minutes until the fish flakes and the prawns are pink.
Remove the bay leaves, add the lemon juice, parsley and black pepper.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: The fish stock is home-made; a stock cube made up with water is saltier. Hake or another firm white fish can replace the cod. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Beef vegetable soup
summary: Slow-simmered beef soup with potatoes, swede, carrots and celery.
method: Cut the stewing beef into 2 cm pieces. Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy saucepan and brown the beef in batches; lift out.
Add the chopped onion, carrots and celery and cook for 8 minutes, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the beef stock, bay leaves and dried thyme, bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the peeled and diced potatoes and swede and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes more until the beef and vegetables are tender. Remove the bay leaves, season with black pepper and stir in the parsley.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Beef stock is made from a cube. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Vegetable and barley stew
summary: Thick stew of pearl barley and root vegetables in a tomato and vegetable stock.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the chopped onion, leek, carrots, celery and parsnip for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, dried thyme, bay leaves and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the rinsed dry pearl barley, then add the chopped tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender.
Add the shredded kale for the last 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and season with black pepper.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: The barley keeps absorbing liquid, so loosen leftovers with a little water. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Chickpea and spinach soup
summary: Cumin-spiced tomato soup with chickpeas and wilted spinach.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes. Mash or blend a few ladles to thicken the soup slightly.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then add the lemon juice and season with black pepper.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Two 400 g tins of chickpeas, drained. Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: Sweetcorn and potato soup
summary: Creamy chowder-style soup of sweetcorn and potato, partly blended.
method: Melt the butter in a large saucepan and soften the chopped onion and celery for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the peeled and diced potatoes and the stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender, then add the frozen sweetcorn and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Blend about two-thirds of the soup until smooth and stir it back in, then add the milk and warm through without boiling. Season with black pepper and scatter with chives if you like.
Serve with the bread if you like.
notes: Bread is optional: about 40 g of Maltese bread a bowl.

name: French onion soup
summary: Slowly caramelised onions in a beef stock and white wine broth, topped with Gruyère toasts.
method: Thinly slice the onions. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large, heavy saucepan, add the onions and cook over a medium-low heat for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Add the sugar after the first 15 minutes to help them colour.

Stir in the garlic, dried thyme and bay leaves for 1 minute, then the plain flour for 1 minute. Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the beef stock. Simmer for 20 minutes and remove the bay leaves.
Slice the baguette, toast the slices under the grill, top with the grated Gruyère and grill until the cheese melts and bubbles.
Season the soup with black pepper, ladle into bowls and float the cheese toasts on top.
notes: Most of the alcohol in the wine cooks off during simmering. The soup freezes well without the cheese toasts.

name: Gazpacho
summary: Chilled blended soup of ripe tomatoes, cucumber and red pepper with olive oil and a little bread.
method: Roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber, red pepper, red onion and garlic. Soak the stale bread in the water for a few minutes.
Blend everything with the olive oil, red wine vinegar and salt until very smooth.
Chill for at least 2 hours, then taste, adjust the vinegar and serve very cold.
notes: Gazpacho-style, made with everyday supermarket ingredients. Best with ripe summer tomatoes.

name: Egg and lemon chicken soup
summary: Chicken and rice soup thickened with whisked egg and lemon, in the style of avgolemono.
method: Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a large saucepan, add the chicken breast and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked through. Lift it out and shred it.
Add the dry rice to the stock and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.

Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice in a bowl. Slowly whisk in two ladles of the hot stock, then pour the mixture back into the pan off the heat, stirring constantly. Warm very gently for 2 to 3 minutes without boiling until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken, season with black pepper and scatter with dill if you like.
notes: Do not let the soup boil once the eggs are in, or they will scramble. Best eaten fresh; reheat gently.
